summary.headline: FY26 revenue rose 29% to INR2,572 crores and EBITDA 22% to INR204 crores; management guides 20-30% profit growth in FY27.
summary.overview: Renaissance Global reported FY26 revenue up about 29-30% YoY to INR2,572 crores, with EBITDA up 22.5% to INR204 crores and PBT before exceptional items up 45% to INR124 crores. Q4 revenue before bullion sales rose 33% to INR686 crores, with EBITDA up 40% to INR57 crores. Growth was led by the US B2C and consumer brands segment, with US D2C revenue up 44% to INR275 crores and D2C EBITDA margin at 12.6%. Gross debt was reduced by about INR120-123 crores in Q4, and management said no dividend will be paid this year. The call was an earnings call with a retail-investor-heavy Q&A, where several questions on share price and dividends went unanswered.

financial_highlights.value: around INR200 crore; total debt INR450 crore; cash plus investments INR200 crore

segments.name: US D2C (Jean Dousset and other brands)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR275 crore (+44%), EBITDA margin 12.6% vs 11.3% in FY25. Management targets organic US D2C growth of 35-40% to INR375 crore by end FY27.

segments.name: Jean Dousset retail
segments.commentary: Two stores currently, each generating about INR30-35 crore annual sales and about INR8-10 crore EBITDA contribution; plan to open 4 more US metro stores in FY27 to reach 6.

segments.name: Licensed brands (Disney fine jewellery)
segments.commentary: Enchanted Disney Fine Jewelry D2C website showing 30-40% organic growth as focus shifts from retail partners to direct-to-consumer.

segments.name: With Clarity (acquired 2022)
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR40 crore four years ago, now almost INR200 crore (about 5x).

guidance_outlook: Profit growth of 20-30% in FY27, cited on the call; separately management said 25-30% annual profit growth for the next 2-3 years.
US D2C revenue to grow organically 35-40% to INR375 crore by end FY27.
D2C ambition of INR1,000 crore revenue by FY29, with D2C EBITDA margins of 15-20%.
Four additional Jean Dousset stores in FY27 across US metropolitan luxury markets, taking the network to 6.
Net debt expected to reach zero within 12-24 months; dividend to start only after zero net debt; buyback possible later but subject to Board approval.
No dividend for the current year, as capex for store expansion and debt repayment take priority.
capex_capacity: Capex needed for Jean Dousset retail store expansion; four new US stores planned in FY27 (second store opened in New York in November 2025).
Approximately INR40 crore annual cost savings achieved in FY26 across sourcing, manufacturing efficiencies and integration.
Debt reduction of roughly INR120-123 crore in Q4 FY26 through working capital management and cash flow.
demand_pricing: Jean Dousset lab-grown diamond engagement rings sell at an average price of about INR8-9 lakh, per management.
US D2C momentum described as strong, with organic growth across brands; no pricing or competition data disclosed.
Currency: gold and diamond inputs bought in USD act as a compensating hedge; INR exposure covered by forward contracts, so management says it is effectively fully hedged.

qa_highlights.question: When will the company be debt-free and what is the current debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said net debt is around INR200 crore, against capital of INR1,550 crore (net debt-to-equity about 0.15-0.2%); there is no specific zero-debt target, but debt will keep being reduced from profits.

qa_highlights.question: Will dividends be paid?
qa_highlights.answer: No dividend for the current year; capex for Jean Dousset store expansion and debt repayment are the priorities. Dividends to start once the company reaches zero net debt.

qa_highlights.question: Will promoters buy back shares?
qa_highlights.answer: A buyback may be considered after zero net debt, but it needs Board consent and would be disclosed in due course.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Jean Dousset expansion plan and market outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Two stores now, each contributing about INR30 crore revenue and INR8-10 crore to the bottom line; four more stores in FY27 would bring the total to 6 by end FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How is currency risk hedged?
qa_highlights.answer: Gold and diamond purchases in USD offset USD revenue; INR exposure is hedged with bank forward contracts, so the company is more or less fully hedged.

qa_highlights.question: What metrics guide inorganic D2C acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Only branded D2C targets at reasonable valuation, underperforming brands where value can be added; past acquisitions (Jay Gems, With Clarity 2022, Jean Dousset 2025) grew 3-5x.

risks_watch: Net debt of around INR200 crore and expected zero net debt in 12-24 months; delivery depends on profit growth and working capital discipline.
Store rollout execution: four new Jean Dousset stores in FY27, each needing capex.
Management declined to comment on share price performance; shareholder confidence and dividend policy remain open questions.

Figures given on the call were inconsistent in places (net debt figures of INR200 crore vs INR200-250 crore; debt of INR120 crore vs INR123 crore; PAT labelled adjusted vs before exceptional items), so reconcile with the filed results.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and D2C momentum, with specific targets for FY27 and FY29. Evasive on share price, buyback and some shareholder questions, where management declined to comment or deferred to the Board.
key_quotes: We expect our U.S. direct-to-consumer revenues to organically grow between 35% to 40% this year to INR375 crores by end of FY '27.
So I think once we get to a zero net debt position, we would commence a dividend distribution for the shareholders.
Our ambition is to build a INR1,000 crores direct-to-consumer brand by FY29, supported by continued expansion of Jean Dousset and growth across our various other brands.

adds.what: 4 additional Jean Dousset US metro luxury stores (network from 2 to 6)

growth.why: Management guides 20-30% profit growth in FY27 and US D2C revenue up 35-40% organically to INR375 crore by end FY27, backed partly by opening 4 Jean Dousset stores and ~INR40 crore FY26 cost savings, but no order book or capacity-level numbers beyond store count, so backing is partial.
